entries.title: Marriage of Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib to Amina

sources.label: Ibn Sayyid al-Nas, 'Uyun al-Athar, vol 1 p.29

sources.quote: آمنة بنت وهب بن عبد مناف بن زهرة بن كلاب وكانت في حجر عمها وهيب بن عبد مناف

opinions.label: al-Tabari — Abdallah ibn Abd al-Muttalib Marries Amina bint Wahb

sources.label: al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, vol 2 p.242
sources.section: ذكر نسب رسول الله ص وذكر بعض أخبار آبائه وأجداده
sources.quote: فخرج به عبد المطلب حتى أتى به وهب بن عبد مناف بن زهرة- ووهب يومئذ سيد بني زهرة سنا وشرفا- فزوجه آمنة بنت وهب

opinions.label: al-Tabari — Abd al-Muttalib and Abdallah Marry in One Sitting

sources.label: al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, vol 2 p.246
sources.section: ذكر نسب رسول الله ص وذكر بعض أخبار آبائه وأجداده
sources.quote: عن أم بكر بنت المسور، أن عبد المطلب جاء بابنه عبد الله، فخطب على نفسه وعلى ابنه، فتزوجا في مجلس واحد، فتزوج عبد المطلب هالة بنت أهيب بن عبد مناف بن زهرة
sources.quote_en: From Umm Bakr bint al-Miswar: Abd al-Muttalib came with his son Abdallah and proposed for himself and for his son, and they married in a single sitting; Abd al-Muttalib married Hala bint Uhayb ibn Abd Manaf ibn Zuhra.

entries.notes: The Monday opinion gives only the weekday, no day or month. WikiShia also says 'Some Shi'a scholars have considered the twelfth of Rabi' I as the date', and that the 12 Rabi I date 'is the basis for practices in Mecca and Medina'. Wikipedia Mawlid adds that 'others contend that the date of Muhammad's birth is unknown'. Wikipedia Year of the Elephant gives the year as 'approximately equating to 570–571 CE' and says 'Some others have placed the Year of the Elephant one or two decades earlier than 570 CE'. The 570 CE in the WikiShia quote dates the destruction of Abraha's army; WikiShia (al-Jahiz) ties the birth to the same year. No Gregorian day given by any source; none computed.

opinions.year_rule: Placed with the Battle of Badr (2 AH), which this section is part of.

opinions.label: Ibn Hisham — chapter: Uthman Stays Behind with Ruqayya During Badr

sources.label: Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya, vol 1 p.678
sources.quote: عثمان بن عفان بن أبي العاص بن أمية ابن عبد شمس، تخلف على امرأته رقية بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فضرب له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بسهمه، قال: وأجري يا رسول الله؟ قال: وأجرك
sources.quote_en: Uthman ibn Affan ibn Abi al-As ibn Umayya ibn Abd Shams stayed behind with his wife Ruqayya, daughter of the Messenger of God, and the Messenger of God gave him his share; he said: And my reward, O Messenger of God? He said: And your reward.

sources.quote: عثمان بن عفان بن أبى العاص ابن أمية بن عبد شمس رضي الله عنه، لم يحضر، تخلف على ابنة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رقية، فضرب له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بسهمه وأجره

sources.quote: عثمان بن عفان خلفه رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - على امرأته رقية بنت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وكانت مريضة فأقام عليها حتى ماتت
sources.quote_en: Uthman ibn Affan, whom the Messenger of God left behind with his wife Ruqayya, daughter of the Messenger of God; she was ill, and he stayed with her until she died.

sources.section: غزوة رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عام الفتح «1»
sources.quote: في عشر مضين من رمضان عام الفتح من المدينة فصام حتى إذا كان بالكديد أفطر
sources.quote_en: Ten days into Ramadan in the year of the Conquest, from Medina; he fasted until, when he was at al-Kadid, he broke his fast
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

entries.title: Al-Abbas Brings Abu Sufyan to the Prophet's Camp

opinions.label: Placed by Gold Ark (AI)
opinions.year_rule: Placed with the Conquest of Mecca, which this source dates to Ramadan 8 AH; this excerpt gives no year.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Abbas Brings Abu Sufyan to the Prophet's Camp

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.220
sources.quote: قلت: هذا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في عشرة آلاف من المسلمين قال: فما الحيلة؟ قال: تركب في عجز هذه البغلة فأستأمن لك
sources.quote_en: I said: This is the Messenger of God with ten thousand Muslims. He said: What is to be done? He said: Ride behind me on this mule and I will seek safe-conduct for you.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Al-Abbas Meets Abu Sufyan at Night

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 1 p.358
sources.section: خبر العباس وقدومه بأبي سفيان وصاحبيه على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
sources.quote: قال: هذا رسول الله في عشرة آلاف من المسلمين، فأسلم، ثكلتك أمك وعشيرتك،
sources.quote_en: He said: This is the Messenger of God with ten thousand Muslims, so accept Islam, may your mother and clan lose you.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Al-Abbas Brings Abu Sufyan to the Prophet

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 2 p.816
sources.quote: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه، قال: لما نزل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمر الظهران، قال العباس بن عبد المطلب: واصباح قريش!
sources.quote_en: From Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of God camped at Marr al-Zahran, al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib said: Woe to Quraysh this morning!
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Tabari — Al-Abbas Brings Abu Sufyan to the Prophet's Camp

sources.label: al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, vol 3 p.52
sources.quote: فقلت: تركب عجز هذه البغلة، فأستأمن لك رسول الله، فو الله لئن ظفر بك ليضربن عنقك، فردفني فخرجت به اركض بغله رسول الله ص نحو رسول الله ص
sources.quote_en: I said: Ride behind me on this mule and I will ask the Messenger of God for safety for you, for by God if he gets hold of you he will strike off your head. So he rode behind me and I set off with him, galloping the mule of the Messenger of God toward the Messenger of God.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text
sources.books_tab: History of the Prophets and Kings

entries.title: Amnesty for Those in Abu Sufyan's House

opinions.label: Placed by Gold Ark (AI)
opinions.year_rule: Placed with the Conquest of Mecca, which this source dates to Ramadan 8 AH; this excerpt gives no year.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Amnesty for the House of Abu Sufyan

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.221
sources.quote: (من دخل دار أبي سفيان فهو آمن). قال أبو سفيان: داري؟! قال: (دارك)، ثم قال: (من أغلق بابه فهو آمن).
sources.quote_en: Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe. Abu Sufyan said: My house? He said: Your house. Then he said: Whoever shuts his door is safe.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Safety Granted to Those in Abu Sufyan's House

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 1 p.361
sources.section: من دخل دار أبي سفيان فهو آمن
sources.quote: فقال العباس: يا رسول الله! إنك قد عرفت أبا سفيان وحبه الشرف والفخر، اجعل له شيئا. قال: نعم! من دخل دار أبي سفيان فهو آمن، ومن أغلق
sources.quote_en: Al-Abbas said: O Messenger of God, you know Abu Sufyan and his love of honour and pride, so give him something. He said: Yes! Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, and whoever closes
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

entries.title: Conversion of Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa

opinions.label: Placed by Gold Ark (AI)
opinions.year_rule: Placed with the Conquest of Mecca, which this source dates to Ramadan 8 AH; this excerpt gives no year.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Conversion of Hakim ibn Hizam Budayl and Jubayr

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.222
sources.quote: قال: وأسلم يومئذ حكيم بن حزام، وبديل بن ورقاء، وجبير بن مطعم.
sources.quote_en: He said: On that day Hakim ibn Hizam, Budayl ibn Warqa and Jubayr ibn Mut'im became Muslim.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Conversion of Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa'

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 1 p.359
sources.section: دخولهم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
sources.quote: فدخلوا عليه، فمكثوا عنده عامة الليل ليستخبرهم، ودعاهم إلى الإسلام، فأسلم حكيم وبديل.
sources.quote_en: They went in to him and stayed with him most of the night while he asked them for news; he invited them to Islam, and Hakim and Budayl accepted Islam.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa Accept Islam

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 2 p.815
sources.quote: وقال: تشهدون أن لا إله إلا الله وأني رسول الله! فأما حكيم وبديل فشهدا
sources.quote_en: He said: Will you bear witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God? Hakim and Budayl bore witness.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

entries.title: Killing of Ibn Khatal at the Ka'ba

opinions.label: Placed by Gold Ark (AI)
opinions.year_rule: Placed with the Conquest of Mecca, which this source dates to Ramadan 8 AH; this excerpt gives no year.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Killing of Ibn Khatal at the Kaba

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.222
sources.quote: فأدرك ابن خطل وهو متعلق بأستار الكعبة فاستبق إليه سعيد بن حريث وعمار بن ياسر فسبق سعيد عمارا فقتله
sources.quote_en: Ibn Khatal was caught clinging to the curtains of the Ka'ba; Sa'id ibn Hurayth and Ammar ibn Yasir raced to him, and Sa'id beat Ammar to him and killed him.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Ibn Khatal Seeks Refuge in the Ka'ba Curtains

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 1 p.387
sources.quote: دخله رعب حتى ما يستمسك من الرعدة، فانتهى إلى الكعبة فنزل، وطرح سلاحه، ودخل بين أستارها.
sources.quote_en: Terror entered him until he could not stop trembling; he reached the Ka'ba, dismounted, threw down his weapons and went in among its curtains.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Execution of Abd Allah ibn Khatal

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 1 p.399
sources.quote: وأخرج أبو برزة الأسلمي عبد الله بن خطل- وهو متعلق بأستار الكعبة- فضرب عنقه بين الركن والمقام.
sources.quote_en: Abu Barza al-Aslami brought out Abd Allah ibn Khatal, who was clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba, and struck his neck between the Corner and the Station.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Order to Kill Ibn Khatal at the Conquest

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 7 p.150
sources.quote: دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم فتح مكة وعلى رأسه المغفر، فلما نزعه جاءه رجل فقال له: ابن خطل متعلق بأستار الكعبة فقال: اقتلوه
sources.quote_en: The Messenger of God entered on the day of the conquest of Mecca with a helmet on his head. When he took it off a man came and said: Ibn Khatal is clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba. He said: Kill him
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Ibn Khatal Hides Among the Kaaba Curtains

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 2 p.826
sources.quote: حتى انتهى إلى الكعبة فنزل عن فرسه، وطرح سلاحه، فأتى البيت فدخل بين أستاره
sources.quote_en: Until he reached the Kaaba, dismounted from his horse, threw down his weapons, came to the House and went in among its curtains.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Abu Barza Kills Ibn Khatal at the Kaaba

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 2 p.859
sources.quote: أخرجت عبد الله بن خطل وهو معلق بأستار الكعبة، فضربت عنقه بين الركن والمقام.
sources.quote_en: I brought out Abd Allah ibn Khatal while he was clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba, and struck off his head between the Corner and the Station.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: Ibn Sa'd — Ibn Khatal Ordered Killed at the Ka'ba

sources.label: Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol 2 p.106
sources.section: غزوة رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عام الفتح «1»
sources.quote: أن أنس بن مالك حدثه أنه رأى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عام الفتح وعلى رأسه المغفر فلما نزعه عن رأسه أتاه رجل
sources.quote_en: Anas ibn Malik told him that he saw the Messenger of God in the year of the Conquest with the helmet on his head; when he took it off, a man came to him
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Tabari — Execution of Abd Allah ibn Khatal

sources.label: al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, vol 3 p.60
sources.quote: واما عبد الله ابن خطل، فقتله سعيد بن حريث المخزومي وأبو برزة الأسلمي، اشتركا في دمه
sources.quote_en: As for Abd Allah ibn Khatal, Sa'id ibn Hurayth al-Makhzumi and Abu Barza al-Aslami killed him, sharing in his blood.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text
sources.books_tab: History of the Prophets and Kings

entries.title: Key of the Ka'ba Brought from Uthman ibn Talha

opinions.label: Placed by Gold Ark (AI)
opinions.year_rule: Placed with the Conquest of Mecca, which this source dates to Ramadan 8 AH; this excerpt gives no year.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — The Key of the Kaba Taken from Umm Shayba

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.224
sources.quote: لما كان فتح مكة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: عند من المفتاح؟ قالوا: عند أم شيبة.
sources.quote_en: When the Conquest of Mecca took place, the Messenger of God said: Who has the key? They said: Umm Shayba has it.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Bilal Sent for the Key of the Kaaba

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 1 p.391
sources.quote: ثم أرسل بلالا إلى عثمان بن طلحة ليأتيه بمفتاح الكعبة فمنعته أمه
sources.quote_en: Then he sent Bilal to Uthman ibn Talha to bring him the key of the Kaaba, but his mother withheld it from him.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Uthman ibn Talha Brings the Key of the Kaaba

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 2 p.832
sources.quote: ثم أرسل بلالا إلى عثمان بن طلحة يأتيه بمفتاح الكعبة، فجاء بلال إلى عثمان
sources.quote_en: Then he sent Bilal to Uthman ibn Talha to bring him the key of the Kaaba, and Bilal came to Uthman.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.226
sources.quote: فبعث غالب بن عبد الله إلى بني مدلج فقالوا: لسنا عليك ولسنا معك
sources.quote_en: He sent Ghalib ibn Abdallah to Banu Mudlij, and they said: We are neither against you nor with you.

entries.title: Amr ibn Umayya Sent to Banu al-Dil

opinions.year_rule: Placed just after the Conquest of Mecca (8 AH), as the excerpt says the raids were sent around Mecca; no year given.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Amr ibn Umayya Sent to Banu al-Dil

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.226
sources.quote: وبعث عمرو بن أمية الضمري إلى بني الديل فدعاهم إلى الله ورسوله فأبوا أشد الإباء

entries.title: Banu Muharib ibn Fihr Accept Islam

opinions.label: Placed by Gold Ark (AI)
opinions.year_rule: Placed just after the Conquest of Mecca (8 AH), as the excerpt says the raids were sent around Mecca; no year given.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Banu Muharib ibn Fihr Accept Islam

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.226
sources.quote: وبعث عبد الله بن سهيل بن عمرو إلى بني محارب بن فهر فأسلموا وجاء معه نفر منهم إلى رسول الله
sources.quote_en: He sent Abdallah ibn Suhayl ibn Amr to Banu Muharib ibn Fihr, and they became Muslim, and some of them came with him to the Messenger of God.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

entries.title: Revelation on Pride in Numbers Before Hunayn

opinions.label: Placed by Gold Ark (AI)
opinions.year_rule: Placed in 8 AH, after the Conquest of Mecca (Ramadan 8 AH in this source) which it follows; the excerpt gives no year.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Revelation on Pride in Numbers Before Hunayn

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.228
sources.quote: فقال أحد أصحابه: لن نغلب اليوم من قلة. فشق ذلك على رسول الله فأنزل الله سبحانه (ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم)
sources.quote_en: One of his companions said: We will not be defeated today for lack of numbers. That troubled the Messenger of God, and God revealed: And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Revelation on Pride in Numbers at Hunayn

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 2 p.10
sources.quote: فقال رجل من بني بكر: لو لقينا بني شيبان ما بالينا، ولا يغلبنا اليوم أحد من قلة! فأنزل الله تعالى: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم
sources.quote_en: A man of Banu Bakr said: If we met Banu Shayban we would not care; no one will defeat us today for lack of numbers! So God revealed: God has helped you on many fields, and on the day of Hunayn when your numbers pleased you.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Revelation on Pride in Numbers Before Hunayn

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 3 p.889
sources.quote: فأنزل الله عز وجل في ذلك: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم
sources.quote_en: So God revealed concerning that: God has helped you on many fields, and on the day of Hunayn when your great number pleased you.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

entries.title: Durayd ibn al-Simma Rebukes Malik ibn Awf

opinions.label: Placed by Gold Ark (AI)
opinions.year_rule: Placed in 8 AH, after the Conquest of Mecca (Ramadan 8 AH in this source) which it follows; the excerpt gives no year.

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Durayd ibn al-Simma Rebukes Malik ibn Awf

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.228
sources.quote: قال: ويحك لم تصنع شيئا، قدمت بيضة (6) هوازن في نحور الخيل، وهل يرد وجه المنهزم شئ؟!
sources.quote_en: He said: Woe to you, you have achieved nothing; you have put the core of Hawazin in front of the horses. Does anything turn back a man in flight?
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Tabari — Durayd ibn al-Simma Questions Malik at Awtas

sources.label: al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, vol 3 p.70
sources.section: ذكر الخبر عن غزوه رسول الله ص هوازن بحنين
sources.quote: فلما نزل بأوطاس، اجتمع إليه الناس، وفيهم دريد بن الصمة في شجار له يقاد به
sources.quote_en: When he camped at Awtas the people gathered to him, among them Durayd ibn al-Simma in a litter of his, being led along.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text
sources.books_tab: History of the Prophets and Kings

entries.title: Muslims Ambushed and Routed at Hunayn

opinions.label: al-Tabrisi — Hawazin Ambush and Rout at Hunayn

sources.label: al-Tabrisi, I'lam al-Wara (Arabic text), vol 1 p.229
sources.quote: قال جابر: فسرنا حتى إذا استقبلنا وادي حنين، كان القوم قد كمنوا في شعاب الوادي ومضائقه، فما راعنا إلا كتائب الرجال بأيديها السيوف والعمد والقني، فشدوا علينا شدة رجل واحد، فانهزم الناس
sources.quote_en: Jabir said: We marched until we faced the valley of Hunayn; the enemy had lain in ambush in the ravines and narrows of the valley. Suddenly squadrons of men with swords, clubs and lances charged us as one man, and the people fled.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: The Prophet Descends into the Valley of Hunayn

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 2 p.12
sources.quote: وانحدر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأصحابه في وادي حنين. وهو على تعبئته وقد ركب بغلته البيضاء دلدل
sources.quote_en: The Messenger of God went down with his companions into the valley of Hunayn in battle order, riding his white mule Duldul.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Rout of the Muslims at Hunayn

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 2 p.12
sources.quote: فاستقبلتهم هوازن في غبش الصبح [ (3) ] بكثرة لم يروا مثلها قط، وحملوا على المسلمين حملة واحدة
sources.quote_en: Hawazin met them in the dark of dawn in numbers they had never seen, and charged the Muslims in a single charge.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Muslims Routed by Ambush at Hunayn

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 3 p.897
sources.quote: إن شعرنا إلا بالكتائب قد خرجت علينا من مضيق الوادي وشعبه فحملوا حملة واحدة، فانكشف أول الخيل- خيل سليم- مولية فولوا
sources.quote_en: We knew nothing until the battalions came out at us from the narrows of the valley and its ravines and charged as one, and the first of the horse, the horse of Sulaym, broke and turned in flight.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: Ibn Sa'd: In Shawwal of the year eight of the Hijra / on the evening of Tuesday night, when ten nights of Shawwal had passed

hijri.text: في شوال سنة ثمان من مهاجر رسول الله / مساء ليلة الثلاثاء لعشر ليال خلون من شوال

opinions.year_rule: The excerpt states the year eight of the Hijra.

sources.label: Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol 2 p.114
sources.section: غزوة رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلى حنين «1»
sources.quote: وخرجت الكتائب من مضيق الوادي وشعبة فحملوا حملة واحدة وانكشفت الخيل خيل بني سليم مولية وتبعهم أهل مكة وتبعهم الناس منهزمين.
sources.quote_en: The squadrons came out of the narrows of the valley and its ravine and charged all at once; the horsemen of Banu Sulaym broke and turned back, the people of Mecca followed them, and the rest followed in flight.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Tabari — Muslims Ambushed and Routed in the Valley of Hunayn

sources.label: al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, vol 3 p.73
sources.section: ذكر الخبر عن غزوه رسول الله ص هوازن بحنين
sources.quote: فو الله ما راعنا ونحن منحطون إلا الكتائب قد شدت علينا شدة رجل واحد، وانهزم الناس أجمعون
sources.quote_en: By God, nothing startled us as we went down but the squadrons charging at us as one man, and the people fled, all of them.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text
sources.books_tab: History of the Prophets and Kings

entries.title: Prophet Throws Pebbles at the Enemy at Hunayn

Wikipedia also: 'Hans Wehr says that the 27th night of the month of Rajab chosen for the Miraj is not based on a report and is an arbitrary choice'. Ibn Sa'd (via Wikipedia) treats Mi'raj (27 Ramadan) and Isra (17 Rabi al-Awwal) as separate events; Wikipedia gives '27th' for Ramadan (checked twice) — other works often cite Ibn Sa'd for 17 Ramadan, so this should be checked against Ibn Sa'd directly. WikiShia also describes an earlier brotherhood pact among Muhajirun in Mecca before the Hijra and a later one in 9 AH; those are separate events and not recorded here. Wikipedia gives no date. No sunnah.com hadith with a date was found. [Note: year added from WikiShia 'Pact of Brotherhood between Muhajirun and Ansar' (first year of Hijra/622; al-Mufid 12 Ramadan 1 AH). sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 2 p.507
sources.quote: فسمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يضحك في السحر فقلت: مم تضحك يا رسول الله، أضحك الله سنك؟ قال: تيب على أبي لبابة.
sources.quote_en: I heard the Messenger of God laughing before dawn and said: What are you laughing at, Messenger of God, may God make you ever smile? He said: Abu Lubaba has been forgiven.

sources.quote_en: From Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt: the acceptance of Abu Lubaba's repentance was revealed to the Messenger of God while he was in the house of Umm Salama.

sources.quote: فلما رأى هؤلاء النفر إباءهم، نزلوا في الليلة التي في صبحها نزلت قريظة، فأسلموا فأمنوا على أنفسهم وأهلهم وأموالهم.
sources.quote_en: When these men saw their refusal, they came down on the night whose morning Qurayza surrendered, embraced Islam, and were safe in their persons, families and property.

opinions.label: Ibn Sa'd — Sons of Sa'ya and Asad ibn Ubayd Embrace Islam

sources.section: ذكر علامات النبوة في رسول الله- صلى الله عليه وسلم - قبل أن يوحى إليه
sources.quote: فلما كان في الليلة التي في صبيحتها فتحت بنو قريظة. قال لهم ثعلبة وأسيد ابنا سعية وأسد بن عبيد فتيان شباب: يا معشر يهود. والله إنه الرجل الذي وصف لنا أبو عمير بن الهيبان. فاتقوا الله واتبعوه.
sources.quote_en: On the night whose morning saw Banu Qurayza conquered, Tha'laba and Usayd the sons of Sa'ya and Asad ibn Ubayd, young men, said to them: O Jews, by God he is the man Abu Umayr ibn al-Hayyiban described to us, so fear God and follow him.

entries.placement: Gold Ark (AI): Banu Hadl (Tha'laba, Usayd, Asad) accepted Islam the night Qurayza surrendered (5 AH); Ibn Hisham only tells it early among the foretellings.

sources.section: (سبب نزول بني قريظة على حكم سعد في رأي ابن هشام) :
sources.quote: أن علي بن أبي طالب صاح وهم محاصرو بني قريظة: يا كتيبة الإيمان، وتقدم هو والزبير بن العوام، وقال: والله لأذوقن ما ذاق حمزة أو لأفتحن حصنهم، فقالوا: يا محمد، ننزل على حكم سعد بن معاذ.
sources.quote_en: Ali ibn Abi Talib cried out while they were besieging Banu Qurayza: O battalion of faith! He and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam advanced, and he said: By God, I will taste what Hamza tasted or I will take their fort. They said: O Muhammad, we will submit to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh.

sources.quote_en: He said: Will you not be content for judgment over them to rest with a man from among you? They said: Yes! He said: Then that is for Sa'd ibn Mu'adh.

sources.quote_en: When the siege exhausted them and they came down to the judgment of the Messenger of God, the Messenger of God ordered their captives bound, and put Muhammad ibn Maslama in charge of binding them.

sources.quote_en: Execution of Banu Qurayza

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi: On Thursday, the seventh of Dhu al-Hijja

hijri.text: في يوم الخميس السابع من ذي الحجة

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 1 p.249
sources.section: خبر بني قريظة بعد حكم سعد وما جرى في قتلهم
sources.quote: ثم غدا صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المدينة في يوم الخميس السابع من ذي الحجة والأسرى معه، وأتى إلى السوق، فأمر بخدود فخدت
sources.quote_en: Then he went early to Medina on Thursday, the seventh of Dhu al-Hijja, with the captives, came to the market, and ordered trenches dug, and they were dug.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Maqrizi — chapter: Execution of the Adult Men of Banu Qurayza

sources.label: al-Maqrizi, Imta' al-Asma', vol 1 p.251
sources.section: قتل كل من أنبت، وبكاء نساء يهود
sources.quote: وأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بقتل كل من أنبت منهم، وترك من لم ينبت، وتمادى القتل فيهم إلى الليل
sources.quote_en: The Messenger of God ordered the killing of every one of them who had reached puberty and left those who had not, and the killing went on among them into the night.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Execution of the Men of Qurayza in the Market

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 2 p.511

sources.quote_en: The Messenger of God sat with the leading men of his companions and called for the men of Banu Qurayza; they were brought out group by group and beheaded.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Waqidi — Execution of the Men of Banu Qurayza

sources.label: al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi, vol 2 p.517

sources.quote_en: From Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: They were killed until the twilight vanished, then the earth was thrown back over them in the trench.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: Ibn Sa'd: Thursday, when seven nights of Dhu al-Hijja had passed

hijri.text: يوم الخميس لسبع ليال خلون من ذي الحجة

sources.quote_en: The Messenger of God left on Thursday, when seven nights of Dhu al-Hijja had passed; then he ordered them brought into Medina, and a trench was dug for them in the market.
sources.check: Arabic quote matched letter for letter in the book text

opinions.label: al-Tabari — Execution of the Men of Banu Qurayza

sources.label: al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, vol 2 p.587

sources.quote_en: He had trenches dug there, then sent for them and beheaded them in those trenches, bringing them out in groups, among them the enemy of God Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn Asad.

entries.notes: The letters were sent at different times, so there is no single date. The WikiShia lead also says: "the majority of accounts place them in the sixth year after the Hijra, following the Treaty of Ḥudaybiyya" (wording of the source, not ours). Wikipedia gives no overall date; its only dated item is the Oman letter (628 AD, the date of the rulers' acceptance, not of sending). Wikipedia says of the letter to the Negus that it is not known whether it went with Ja'far on the migration to Abyssinia "or at a later date following the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah". islamqa answer 36861 was checked and states no date.

entries.notes: Departure from Medina and entry into Mecca are dated separately. Wikipedia's table of ancient sources assigns: Ibrahim — entry 10 Ramadan; Abu Sa'id al-Khudri — departure 2 Ramadan, entry 17/18 Ramadan; al-Hakam — departure 6 Ramadan; Ibn 'Abbas and Tabari — departure 10 Ramadan; Ibn Ishaq — entry 20 Ramadan; Waqidi — departure Wednesday 10 Ramadan; Ibn Sa'd — departure Wednesday 10 Ramadan, entry Friday 19 Ramadan (the table spells the name 'ibd Sad'). Wikipedia states 'Ancient sources vary as to the dates of these events' and gives several Gregorian conversions; it also notes 'Shaikh places the departure on Wednesday, 29 November.' WikiShia quotes for 13 and 20 Ramadan give no year inside the quote, so year is left empty there (the article's infobox gives 8/630). The phrase 'most Shi'a and Sunni scholars' is WikiShia's own wording. Wikipedia URL is used with more than one quote because the values sit in different parts of the article.

entries.notes: Both sources agree on 10 Shawwal 8 AH for the arrival. Wikipedia says 'Wednesday night', WikiShia says 'evening of Tuesday'; these may describe the same evening (the Arabic day begins at sunset) but that is not stated by either source, so both are kept as written. WikiShia's own Gregorian dates conflict: it gives January 27, 630 for 6 Shawwal and December 2, 630 for 10 Shawwal, which cannot both be right — check before use. Wikipedia gives no Gregorian day.

entries.notes: Every source fetched puts Ibrahim's death in 10 AH, not within 6–9 AH; no source giving 8 or 9 AH for the death was found. WikiShia gives birth 8 AH and death 10 AH (10/631). Months differ: Shawwal (Wikipedia infobox) vs Rabi al-Awwal (Ibn Kathir via Wikipedia; WikiShia). Gregorian years differ: 632 (Wikipedia) vs 631 (WikiShia). Wikipedia's January 27, 632 rests on modern astronomical tables for the eclipse; the 'Muhammad's eclipse' article only says the eclipse was 'around the time' of Ibrahim's death. Ages at death: Wikipedia 'at the age of 2'; WikiShia 'sixteen months', 'eighteen months', or per Ibn Shahrashub 'one year, ten months and eight days'; 'Muhammad's eclipse' article '18 months old'. The WikiShia URL Ibrahim_b._Rasul_Allah_(s) was blocked; Ibrahim_b._Muhammad worked. No sunnah.com hadith fetched here; the eclipse hadiths link the eclipse to the day of death but were not checked for a date.

entries.notes: Bukhari 45 is about the verse 'This day I have perfected your religion' (5:3); it gives Friday at Arafat but no day number or year. WikiShia derives Wednesday from Imam al-Sadiq's narration that Eid al-Ghadir (18 Dhu l-Hijja) was Friday; the same WikiShia section also says 'the Second Caliph is said to have reported that staying in 'Arafat was made on Friday.' WikiShia's 10 AH page says Quran 5:3 was revealed at Ghadir (see GL-E-04), a differing view on the verse.

Age opinions and weekday-only opinions have no calendar date, so all date fields are null and precision is 'traditional'. Wikipedia's 'aged 61–62' (infobox, inside the 8 June 632 quote) is a further age figure. WikiShia notes the Shia historian Rasul Ja'farian says no narration directly supports 28 Safar. Gregorian equivalents differ by source (May 25 for 28 Safar; June 7 per WikiShia and June 8 per Wikipedia for the Sunni date); not reconciled. al-islam.org page also contains the line 'In the 10th year of Hijrat, he passed away on 28th Safar' (year as written there; not used). Year 11 AH: islamqa says 'there is no difference of opinion' that it was 11 AH; WikiShia lead says '11 AH/632 CE'. Same source URL appears in more than one opinion here (different quote each) because one page lists several opinions.
